# Reading the QC dashboard

When the Core workflow finishes, `output/qc/MicroC_qc_report.html` is the
first thing to open. It is one self-contained file (the plotting library is
embedded), so it works offline, and you can email it. It has one section per
question you would ask about a library. This chapter says what each panel
shows, how to read it, and what a failing Micro-C library looks like.

::: {.callout-warning}
**The thresholds are rules of thumb.** The pass / warn / fail cut-offs are
the defaults of `qc_thresholds` in `config/MicroCConfig.yaml`. They were
chosen for this pipeline, are not published standards, and depend on your
cell type, protocol and sequencing. Compare a new library with your own
good ones, and adjust the config to match.
:::

Everything is computed from the `pairtools dedup` statistics of each group
(`{group}_dedup_stats.txt`), plus the preseq output and benchmark files when
they exist. Groups whose stats file is missing are left out.

## Summary table

One row per group, sortable by column. Each metric cell is coloured by its
status, and the group's status is its worst metric. Hover a column header for
the definition and the thresholds.

| Metric | Definition | Direction |
|--------|-----------|-----------|
| Mapped (%) | mapped read pairs / total read pairs | higher is better |
| Duplicates (%) | duplicate read pairs / total read pairs | lower is better |
| Cis (%) | cis pairs / non-duplicate pairs | higher is better |
| Cis >= 1 kb (%) | cis pairs of at least 1 kb / non-duplicate pairs | higher is better |
| Cis < 1 kb (%) | cis pairs shorter than 1 kb / non-duplicate pairs | lower is better |
| Cis >= 10 kb (%) | cis pairs of at least 10 kb / non-duplicate pairs | higher is better |
| Unique pairs (M) | non-duplicate pairs, in millions | higher is better |

Three more columns are informational and have no traffic light: total pairs
(M), duplicates as a share of mapped pairs, and valid pairs (trans plus
cis >= 1 kb, as a share of non-duplicate pairs, the same definition as in
Dovetail's `get_qc.py`).

The same numbers, in a plain table, are in
`output/{group}/{group}_qc_summary.txt`.

### Default thresholds

| Metric | warn | fail |
|--------|------|------|
| Mapped | below 80 | below 60 |
| Duplicates | above 40 | above 60 |
| Cis | below 70 | below 50 |
| Cis >= 1 kb | below 40 | below 25 |
| Cis < 1 kb | above 40 | above 55 |
| Cis >= 10 kb | below 20 | below 10 |
| Unique pairs (M) | below 100 | below 20 |

A value exactly on an edge is not penalised.

## What the metrics mean for Micro-C

- **Mapped and duplicates.** Low mapping suggests contamination, the wrong
  reference, adapters or very short reads. High duplicates mean the library
  was sequenced past its complexity (see the preseq panel) or too little
  material went into the PCR. Duplicates are a share of *all* read pairs.
- **Cis versus trans.** Most real contacts are between loci on the same
  chromosome. A low cis share (high trans) points to random ligation
  between unrelated fragments, the usual signature of a noisy library.
- **Cis < 1 kb versus >= 1 kb.** This is the most Micro-C-specific check.
  Very short cis pairs include real nucleosome-scale contacts but also
  uninformative products (undigested, self-ligated or dangling fragments)
  that carry no long-range information. A library whose cis pairs are
  mostly < 1 kb has little information per sequenced read, however many
  reads there are. The share >= 1 kb, and especially >= 10 kb, is what
  feeds the loops, domains and compartments you will analyse.
- **Unique pairs.** Absolute depth of the final `.pairs.gz`. Needed
  depth depends on the resolution you want: fine bins need many more
  pairs than coarse ones.

## Library composition

- **Pair types.** Stacked bars of the `pairtools` pair types as a share of
  all read pairs: `UU` unique-unique (the good ones), `UR` / `RU` rescued,
  `NU` / `UN` one side unmapped, `MU` one side multi-mapped, `DD`
  duplicates, and so on. A large unmapped or multi-mapped slice explains a low
  mapped %; a large `DD` slice explains the duplicate %. (If the stats file
  has no pair types, the panel falls back to unmapped / duplicates /
  non-duplicate.)
- **Cis vs trans.** Cis and trans shares of non-duplicate pairs.
- **Cis by genomic distance.** Stacked bars of cis pairs split into
  distance bins (< 1 kb, 1-2, 2-4, 4-10, 10-20, 20-40 and >= 40 kb) plus trans. Compare libraries
  here: a good library puts a large share in the longer bins.
- **Contact matrices (.mcool).** Only if `cooler` can be imported: number
  of resolutions, finest bin, contacts, non-zero pixels and whether the
  matrix is balanced.

## Contact decay P(s)

P(s) is the contact probability as a function of the genomic distance s
between the two read ends. The panel plots, for every group, pairs per base
pair of distance (normalised so that curves are comparable regardless of
depth) on log-log axes, with a dashed line at 1 kb.

- **Beyond ~1 kb** the curve should fall smoothly, roughly as a power law;
  loops, domains and the cell cycle bend it gently, so replicates of the same
  cell type should lie nearly on top of each other.
- **Below ~1 kb** Micro-C shows nucleosome-scale features (the
  "shoulder") that restriction-enzyme Hi-C cannot resolve. A library that
  has no sign of it, or whose short-range part dominates and differs sharply
  from its replicates, deserves a closer look.
- **Outliers.** A curve that sits well above its replicates at short range
  and below them at long range is a library dominated by short products.
  A curve that flattens at long range suggests excess random ligation.

## Strand orientation versus distance

For each distance bin, the fraction of pairs that are inward-facing, outward-
facing, or on the same strand, divided by what random ligation would give
(25% inward, 25% outward, 50% same-strand). So a value of 1 means balanced.

- **At long range** all three lines should sit near 1.
- **At short range** a strong excess of inward or outward pairs flags
  artefacts: undigested DNA, self-ligated fragments, or dangling ends.
  Some short-range deviation is expected in Micro-C, because the geometry
  of ligation between neighbouring nucleosomes is not random; what matters
  is that it resolves toward 1 with distance, and that replicates agree.

## Library complexity

The curve is `preseq lc_extrap`: for a given number of sequenced read pairs,
how many *distinct* pairs you would expect, with a 95% confidence band. The
diamond marks what was actually observed (mapped reads versus non-duplicate
pairs from `pairtools`); a small offset from the curve is expected, because
preseq counts reads in the BAM.

- A curve that is still rising steeply at your depth says more sequencing
  will pay off.
- A curve that has flattened says you are mostly resequencing the same
  molecules, and new depth should come from a new library.

`preseq_extrap` in the config sets how far the curve is extrapolated. The
panel is empty if `library_complexity` is turned off.

## Runtime and memory

A table, one row per group and rule, of wall time, peak memory (RSS) and I/O,
read from the benchmark files. Use it to size your profile: if `hic` or `dedup`
peaked near its memory limit, raise it before the next, deeper library.
The same data is in `output/benchmarking.tsv`.

## Methods

The last section lists every metric's definition with the **active**
thresholds, and describes each plot, so a shared report is self-explanatory.

## What failure looks like

| What you see | Likely cause | What to do |
|--------------|--------------|------------|
| Low mapped %, many `NN` / `NU` pairs | Wrong reference or chromosome sizes, adapter or contamination, reads too short | Check `fasta`, `chromSizes`, read length; look at the unmapped reads |
| High duplicates, preseq curve flat | Over-sequenced low-complexity library | Make or sequence a new library; deeper sequencing of this one adds little |
| Low cis %, high trans | Random ligation, poor crosslinking or digestion | Library is noisy; consider repeating the prep |
| Most cis pairs < 1 kb | Over-digested or under-ligated chromatin; short, uninformative products | Few useful long-range contacts per read; check the prep rather than adding depth |
| Strong short-range orientation excess that does not fade with distance | Undigested or self-ligated fragments | As above |
| Good percentages but very few unique pairs | Fine, just shallow | Sequence deeper (see preseq) |
| P(s) of a replicate disagrees with its siblings | Different digestion level, or a failed library | Do not merge it blindly |

A warning is not a verdict: libraries that warn can still be informative at
coarser resolution. A failure on `cis_ge1kb_pct` or on unique pairs is the
most consequential for loop-scale analysis.

## Changing thresholds or rebuilding the dashboard

Edit `qc_thresholds` in your config and rebuild only the
dashboard:

```bash
bash MicroCPipe.sh --forcerun qc_report
```

The dashboard step reads the config file the run was started with
(`--configfile`, else `config/MicroCConfig.yaml`) and waits for
`benchmarking.tsv`; to hide it entirely set `qc_report: false`.
